title: Brentford 4-0 Everton: Moyes' milestone game ends in humbling defeat
subtitle: Brentford surged into sixth place in the Premier League as they ran riot against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.
paragraphs: David Moyes' record-breaking match in charge of Everton turned out to be one to forget as James Tarkowski's red card compounded a 4-0 defeat to Brentford.

Tarkowski received the first red card of his Premier League career, in his 351st match in the top flight, in the 40th minute at the Gtech Community Stadium, where Moyes was overseeing his 593rd Everton game.
By that stage, Everton were already 2-0 down, with Keane Lewis-Potter having scored twice in the space of 178 seconds to put Brentford deservedly in control.
Keith Andrews was without key players Nathan Collins and Igor Thiago, yet Brentford were as brilliant as Everton were poor.

Jaidon Anthony and Mikkel Damsgaard fired warning shots before Callum Wilson – a consistent tormentor of Everton down the years – teed up Michael Kayode, who skewed wide when one-on-one with Jordan Pickford.

The pressure told in the 23rd minute as Anthony deftly helped a looping pass into the path of Lewis-Potter, whose shot deflected in off Jarrad Branthwaite to open the scoring and mark Brentford's 300th Premier League goal.
Lewis-Potter doubled up less than three minutes later, as he drilled home at the second attempt via a deflection off Thierno Barry, with Everton failing to clear their lines from a set-piece.
Everton's task was made even harder when Tarkowski, after a VAR review, received a straight red card for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin.
Birthday boy Caoimhin Kelleher pulled off a fantastic save to deny Barry in Everton's first opportunity right at the end of the first half.
Yet there was never really any danger of an Everton comeback, and their hopes were quashed in the 67th minute when Vitaly Janelt fired a long-range piledriver into the top-right corner.
And Brentford's surge into sixth place was capped off when Fabio Carvalho came off the bench to bundle in from Mathias Jensen's corner in the 90th minute.
Brentford bounce back on bad day at the office for Everton
Andrews' team went into the international break on the back of a 2-0 loss to Brighton, in which star striker Thiago was sent off.

Brentford had won just one of their last 11 Premier League games that have come the matchday following an international break (D5 L5), but they put that record to rest with a dominant showing from start to finish, claiming their biggest league win under Andrews.

They were certainly helped by a well below-par Everton performance, and Moyes will now have to rally his troops, who will be missing club captain Tarkowski, for Sunday's Merseyside derby clash with Liverpool.
Brentford have now won five of their last eight league home games, though this is the first time they have won back-to-back top-flight matches at the Gtech Community Stadium in 2026.

The Bees have never lost a Premier League game when leading by 2+ goals (P53 W51 D2), while Everton have now lost their last 41 such matches in the competition, since a survival-sealing 3-2 comeback win over Crystal Palace in May 2022.
Brentford finished having amassed 21 shots, worth a combined 2.77 expected goals, while Everton generated only 0.23 xG from a meagre four attempts.
